item.title: Braves Lefty Suter Signs $4 Million Deal With Yankees
item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Relief pitcher Brent Suter is heading to New York. The left-hander, who pitched well for the Braves late in the 2026 season, signed a one-year contract worth $4 million with the Yankees. This move ends his time in Atlanta and adds a proven arm to the Bronx Bombers’ bullpen. The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported the deal on Tuesday, confirming Suter will not return to the team that traded for him in August. Suter arrived at the trade deadline from the Angels in exchange for infielder Nacho Alvarez Jr. He made an immediate impact with the Braves, posting a 2-0 record and a 1.63 ERA across 13 regular season games. His work did not stop there. During the National League Division Series versus the Dodgers, he also played in two contests, pitching three scoreless innings. Despite these strong numbers, the Braves chose not to keep him for the 2027 season. A Reluctant Loss for Atlanta The Braves have seen this before. Suter is now the first notable free agent from the 2026 roster to sign elsewhere. Other pitchers like Tyler Mahle and Martín Pérez remain unsigned, along with infielder Mauricio Dubón and closer Raisel Iglesias. However, losing a lefty with Suter’s recent track record hurts. He was a steady hand in high-leverage spots when the team needed him most. The decision to let him walk suggests the front office is looking to save money or believes other arms are ready to step up. Either way, the Yankees just gained a player who knows how to get outs in the playoffs. The $4 million price tag reflects his value. It is a fair sum for a veteran lefty who can eat innings and keep the ball in the park. The Yankees are known for spending to fill gaps, and this signing fits their pattern. They needed depth after a long season, and Suter provides exactly that. For Atlanta, the loss is not just about the numbers. It is about the stability he offered in a bullpen that often gets tested. The team now has to find someone else to fill that role without the benefit of Suter’s experience. The NL East Shifts Again The division is getting harder to navigate. While the Braves lose Suter, the New York Mets are making massive moves of their own. Tarik Skubal signed a record nine-year, $450 million deal with the Mets, according to Yahoo Sports . This is the largest pitching contract in league history. The Mets are clearly trying to dominate the division by spending big. Now the Yankees are adding Suter to their mix. The distance separating the leading clubs from the others is expanding rapidly. Atlanta cannot ignore this level of spending from its rivals. The Braves know Skubal well. He played two games against Atlanta in the regular season with a 4.91 ERA. Over 6.0 innings in a single playoff matchup, he recorded a 1.50 ERA while striking out 7 batters. item.title: What Peugeot had planned for its abandoned 2027 WEC Hypercar
item.description: Motorsport photo The 2027-spec 9X8 LMH was set to offer Peugeot its best chance of becoming a consistent World Endurance Championship frontrunner against some stiff Hypercar competition. The French manufacturer had invested considerable resources into developing a revised version of the car that had fallen short of the expectations set by its predecessor, the 908 LMP1. This would have been the third major iteration of the V6-powered challenger, following a previous update in 2024 that failed to yield the desired results. By mid-2025, Peugeot had already identified several key weaknesses with the package. Even after being granted the lowest weight and the maximum power under the Balance of Performance adjustments, the 9X8 was simply not competitive enough against the likes of Toyota, Porsche and Ferrari . Peugeot felt that incremental refinements alone would not be enough, with the car having reached a performance ceiling that engineers struggled to overcome. While Peugeot initially considered ditching the 9X8 entirely in favour of a clean-sheet design, even holding talks with the WEC’s promoters – to understand if this would be allowed, it eventually chose to update its existing car instead. The French manufacturer had its hands tied in 2026, having already exhausted its original allocation of five evo jokers and the second homologation. So it spent the year struggling largely at the back of the pack, while its engineers simultaneously began working on overhauling the package for 2027, with a new rule granting struggling manufacturers two additional evo updates during their cars' life cycles. Crucially, the update Peugeot had planned for 2027 wasn’t about undoing the damage caused by the convergence of the LMH and LMDh regulations – something that had significantly compromised the original design of the car. Instead, it was aimed at tackling the specific shortcomings of the second-generation 9X8, including its notoriously poor performance at the Le Mans 24 Hours. As with other manufacturers introducing evo updates, aerodynamics was the key focus of development for the Satory-based brand. But it was also working on several other changes under the hood to improve the cornering performance of the 9X8. #94 Peugeot Totalenergies Peugeot 9X8: Loic Duval #94 Peugeot Totalenergies Peugeot 9X8: Loic Duval “In terms of development of the car, the key targets were to eradicate the issues we had with the current package,” team principal Emmanuel Esnault explained at Monza earlier this month. “So, meaning in terms of [aero] dumping [to improve straightline performance] and in terms of aero consistency; these were the key words. “The main handicaps we had were the aerodynamic balance variation on the three phases that make up a corner; that is the entry, the middle of the corner and the exit. “And the [other area of focus was] control of the platform, which is the damping of the suspension. item.description: ATLANTA, GA - JULY 31: Starting pitcher Foster Griffin (22) of the Washington Nationals stares down a hitter during the Friday evening MLB game between the Atlanta Braves and the Washington Nationals on July 31, 2026 at Truist Park in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by David J. Griffin/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The starting pitching market in free agency is moving very quickly. After Tarik Skubal signed his historic deal with the Mets, the floodgates have opened. We have seen the likes of Freddy Peralta, Kaima Taira, Trevor Rogers and Kris Bubic sign in the past 48 hours. That means the Nats will have to act quickly if they want to get a starter. One option for Paul Toboni could be a reunion with Foster Griffin. Last offseason the Nats signed Griffin to a 1-year $5.5 million deal. He had spent the last three years pitching very well in Japan. The bargain paid off, with Griffin becoming an All-Star. At the trade deadline, the Nats cashed in, flipping the lefty to Cleveland. As all Nats fans know, Griffin succeeds due to his command and deep arsenal. The 31 year old southpaw throws 7 pitches, and has full faith in all of them. Right away, Nats fans knew he was legit when he struck out the side against the Dodgers using three different pitches. item.title: Confirmed: Fermin Lopez hit with two-match ban; will miss Deportivo, Atletico Madrid games
item.description: Confirmed: Fermin Lopez hit with two-match ban; will miss Deportivo, Atletico Madrid games In what comes as a blow for Barcelona, key midfielder Fermin Lopez has been hit with a two-match suspension following his red card against Villarreal last Sunday. As a result, the in-form 23-year-old will miss the team’s La Liga matches against Deportivo de A Coruna and Atletico Madrid over the coming week. What happened? Fermin was sent off by referee Hernandez Hernandez while being seated on the Barcelona bench in the second half during the 3-2 win over Villarreal. It emanated from the La Masia graduate, who had scored on the day before being subbed off, voicing his protest over a potential penalty decision not going the Catalans’ way for a foul on Anthony Gordon. Fermin was sent off against Villarreal. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The referee recorded the incident in his report, stating that the midfielder had left the dugout and approached the fourth official at close range while protesting loudly. The referee specifically noted that Fermin repeatedly used the expression “Don’t f**k with me!” during the exchange. Two-match ban Barcelona were hoping that the youngster would get away with only a one-match suspension. However, the Disciplinary Committee has classified the incident as a protest under Article 127 of the Disciplinary Code. The regulation provides for a suspension of between two and three matches, or a ban of up to one month, for protesting against the referee, assistant referees or fourth official when the conduct does not constitute a more serious offence. Two-match ban for Fermin. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Fermin has now received the minimum suspension under the article: two matches. Barcelona had submitted an appeal in an attempt to challenge the decision, but they were not accepted. The suspension means the midfielder will be unavailable for Barcelona’s visit to Deportivo at Riazor this Sunday. The more significant absence comes next Wednesday, when Barcelona host Atletico Madrid at the Spotify Camp Nou – a fixture that was initially scheduled for January but brought forward due to the Spanish Super Cup scheduling. Barcelona have little room to challenge the decision successfully through the Appeals Committee as the disciplinary body has imposed the lowest punishment available under the relevant regulation, which makes the prospect of reducing the suspension limited. Source: Mundo Deportivo

item.title: Cut the Grass: After Mexico City, the 49ers Get Back to Work in the NFC West
item.description: On December 1, 2001, my Bowie High School team beat Eleanor Roosevelt 23-6 at Byrd Stadium for the first state championship in school history. We were the sixth seed. Roosevelt was undefeated and had beaten us in September. They had won nine straight against us, going back to 1994. We scored the first 23 points. When it was over, one of my teammates walked off that field with a plastic bag full of grass—a souvenir. I got home late that night. My parents were proud, but they kept it simple: Be safe, and be home when we wake up. The next morning, I was in church. I even got a shout-out from the pulpit. And that afternoon, I was in the yard cutting the grass, because the playoff run had put me behind on my chores. Took me years to understand it, but the trophy and the lawnmower were the same lesson. The habits that won the championship were the same ones that had me cutting grass the next day. Sunday night in Mexico City was the 49ers’ championship night. A 35-10 win over the best defense in football, in prime time, on an international stage. By Monday, they were Super Bowl favorites, and Brock Purdy’s MVP odds had jumped from +400 to +210. Then Kyle Shanahan was asked if this is the best team he’s coached in San Francisco. “No, but it’s still early,” he said. “We’ve got to earn that.” Now it’s back to the yard. It’s been 49 days since the 49ers played a division game, and the last one took just about everything they had. Seven turnovers between the two teams. Six lead changes. The 49ers hadn’t scored a touchdown against Seattle in more than eight quarters until Mike Evans caught a 2-yarder less than four minutes in. Renardo Green picked off Sam Darnold twice. Fred Warner punched a ball loose, Malik Mustapha fell on it, and Christian McCaffrey scored on the next snap. With 13 seconds left in the half, G-Baby, rookie Gracen Halton, stripped George Holani and recovered it in the end zone. Then Seattle scored 13 straight in the third quarter, and the 49ers had to go get it. Down 26-21, they went 74 yards in 12 plays, and Evans caught a 28-yarder on second-and-21 to set up the go-ahead touchdown. The winning field goal came at the end of a drive built on five runs for 36 yards, and Seattle’s last shot died when Cooper Kupp came up short on fourth-and-10 at midfield. That’s what the division looks like. Ugly, physical, and decided by inches. And the 49ers walking into Levi’s on Sunday aren’t the same team that left Seattle. G-Baby broke his ankle against the Raiders. Right tackle Colton McKivitz is out for the year, and Vederian Lowe, who has played 1,415 career snaps at left tackle and only 276 on the right, takes his place. Nick Bosa missed that first meeting, and DeForest Buckner was still a Colt. Both are back. Purdy has gone 43-for-54 with six touchdowns and no interceptions in his last two games, and the offense has averaged 32.4 points since that trip to Seattle. The Seahawks are different, too. item.title: Man behind the curtain calling entertainment plays at Polar Park
item.description: WORCESTER – While fans watch the players sweep through the field, sing along to classics and new hits, and wait for their sick moves to appear on the jumbotron, there is a man sitting behind a curtain making it all happen. Actually, there are several. Many people go to the ballpark to watch the game, but it is not the only interesting thing happening there. From music to the kiss cam, the Worcester Red Sox Entertainment Department helps turn baseball into a full night out at Polar Park. Without the technology that has become a regular part of the modern-day ballpark experience, this job would look significantly different. Before video boards became a regular feature, scoreboards were used for the minimum: the score, the inning and the lineup. That changed in 1980 when Dodger Stadium introduced the first full-color video board during the All-Star Game. This technology opened up new opportunities for entertainment beyond the game. Over time, video boards brought replays, highlights, promotional videos and crowd-participation features. According to Fun While it Lasted, a website that documents the history of sports, when the Pawtucket Red Sox – rebranded as the Worcester Red Sox – moved to Worcester in 2021, the franchise significantly stepped up its technology game. Polar Park was built with five boards, including two large video screens. It was a huge change from McCoy Stadium, which had been referred to as “a dump” by Ben Mondor, a retired mill owner who became the Pawtucket Red Sox’s third owner in the '70s. Westborough native at the controls For Brendan Black, a longtime baseball fan who grew up in Westborough, those large screens were wildly important. He is the director of ballpark entertainment. Black began working for the team in 2021 as a videographer before moving into a producer role in 2023. His job took root at age 10, when he was first interested in photography and videography, eventually teaching himself how to edit videos. After studying communications at the University of New Hampshire, he found himself working in sales to pay the bills. It was a relief when the WooSox came along, opening up an opportunity for him. “It just so happened that these two worlds of mine kind of collided,” Black said, recalling what it was like to bring together two interests that had followed him for years – baseball and entertainment. But putting on a show takes more than making a playlist and pressing "play." On game days, the work begins long before the fans fill the seats. At 10 a.m., the team holds what Black calls a “DOG” meeting – short for Day of Game. The staff goes over the weather, expected crowd size, ticket blocks and any promotions planned. The hours before the game are spent preparing material needed for that night. That can include graphics, sponsors, pregame ceremonies, themed events and updating player information. item.title: John Motson’s legendary voice resurrected by AI for EA FC 27
item.description: Legendary football commentator John Motson‘s voice is set to return to EA FC 27 through the use of AI - three years after his death. Motson, who died aged 77 in 2023 , worked on the BBC ’s flagship Match of the Day programme since 1971 and covered more than 2,000 televised games, including 29 FA Cup finals and 10 World Cups. He retired from live commentary in 2008 but continued to work on Match of the Day programme until he hung up the microphone in 2018. EA Sports said they worked with John Motson’s family to bring back his iconic voice in a “digital tribute” through the use of new AI-tools, “bringing a mix of both his original audio and an AI-recreation trained by recordings of the man himself”. The commentator featured in EA Sports’ annual FIFA game series from 1996 to 2006. John Motson featured in EA Sports’ annual FIFA game series from 1996 to 2006 A studio spokesperson said EA Sports have “worked with extensive care and respect to create a digital tribute to one of the game’s greatest voices, inspiring a whole new generation of football fans.” “My father adored being the voice of the game, and we are so grateful to the team at EA SPORTS FC for this touching tribute and preserving his memory in-game,” said Fred Motson, son of John Motson. “His voice inspired millions of players across generations every time they picked up a controller, and now a whole new set of fans will get to experience his legacy and commentary.” After starting as a newspaper reporter in Barnet and at the Sheffield Morning Telegraph , Motson joined the BBC in 1968 as a sports presenter on Radio 2. His long career also took in two Olympic Games and Wimbledon’s memorable 1988 FA Cup final triumph against Liverpool at Wembley, as the Crazy Gang beat the Culture Club. Awarded the OBE in 2001 for services to broadcasting, Motson hung up his microphone for the BBC at the end of the 2017-18 Premier League season. EA Sports football game series began in 1994 with the release of FIFA International Soccer, with the FIFA name continuing until 2023, when the termination of EA and FIFA’s licensing agreement led to the 2024 game being called FC. John Motson’s voice will be added to EA in Title Update v1.3.0 on 26 November as an optional commentary selection.

item.title: Charley Hull brings laughs, nerves and a wink to highly anticipated WTGL debut
item.description: PALM BEACH GARDENS, Fla. — Atlanta Drive's Charley Hull stood in a bunker at SoFi Center holding a conversation with team owner Arthur Blank. Hull, whose team would make its WTGL debut about 30 minutes later, then grabbed her wedge, and as Blank was walking away, holed a 30-footer. Looking on and nodding with approval was Billy Horschel, a star on Atlanta's TGL team. For Hull — and Atlanta — that proved to be the highlight of the night. Even with Horschel and Justin Thomas, both part of Atlanta's championship winning team in TGL's inaugural season, lending support from the team owner's box, Boston Common Golf defeated Atlanta, 8-3, Tuesday at SoFi Center. Boston Common had the advantage of playing its second WTGL match. "Obviously it wasn't the result that we wanted, but we had a great laugh," Hull said in perhaps the most upbeat post-game press conference ever held by a losing team. "It is a lot of fun. It's nice actually to be ... I know we're not on the golf course, but you're in the golf environment, and having a laugh." Hull, one of the marquee names playing in WTGL's first season, is considered the most popular active women's golfer in Europe. The Englishwoman is No. 7 in the world, a three-time winner on the LPGA Tour and although she still is chasing her first major championship, she has five runner-ups in the tour's marquee events. She has played in eight Solheim Cups. Hull, 30, also this year checked off what she called a childhood dream, appearing in the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit edition. All of which makes her a natural for a league that encourages the golfers to let loose and show their personality. Her 869,000 Instagram followers are more than any other golfer on WTGL's 25-woman roster. "I think it's cool that here in WTGL we can expose people that it's actually fun to play golf and dress pretty cool," said Hull's teammate, Nataliya Guseva. "I think that's kind of our goal as well with Charley out here with the Malbon (golf fashion) stuff." Every woman who has played in the league's first four matches agrees the league is part entertainment and fashion along with the competition. Guseva, the 23-year-old Russian, had a rough night, drawing three penalties. She admitted to having nerves and said ... well, here is what she said. "It was super cool, but it was just kind of weird ... to show how nervous I am," she said. "But at the same time, every golfer kind of has nerves, and I think it's kind of cool to show that even professional golfers kind of s*** themselves during a tournament." "Yeah, I think it was great." Charley Hull's WTGL debut: A lot of laughs in Atlanta's loss From the entertainment side, Hull's debut was as expected. item.title: Penn State offense, Maryland defense are evenly matched
item.description: This has been a challenging season for Penn State’s offense to say the least. Instead of a consistently productive unit that improved as the season went along, they’ve presented a disjointed operation that excels one week and is left searching for answers the next week. The ebbs and flows of the season have been aggressive, even in individual games. A staple of the Nittany Lions offense has been jumping out to double-digit leads in the first half, and then completely falling apart in the second half, whether it be from turnovers or just a lack of execution. Maryland doesn’t have a great defense, but Penn State recently showed that even the worst defenses — like the Rutgers Scarlet Knights — can have success against it. The offense for the blue and white could score 40 points this week, or they could barely hit 20 points and be in a dog fight late in the fourth quarter. It’s impossible to know which version of the Nittany Lions will show up from week to week, but here are the raw numbers about the unit compared to the Terrapins defense. Turnovers Penn State offense: 9 turnovers Maryland defense: 15 takeaways Turnovers have the biggest indicator of whether Penn State will win this season. The team is 6-0 when it doesn’t turn the ball over, and 5-0 when it turns the ball over at all. The Nittany Lions have been one of the best teams in terms of taking care of the ball, currently tied for 18th in the nation with just nine giveaways. This means that the Terrapins aren’t great on that side of the ball, but they also aren’t a pushover. item.description: Free agent utilityman Mauricio Dubon The Baltimore Orioles signed Freddy Peralta to a five-year, $125 million deal, but they may not be done adding to their team. The Orioles could use some help on offense, and according to The Athletic's Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon , they are showing interest in Mauricio Dubón, among other players. Dubón is an interesting target for any team. He is a versatile defender who can play all over the field and is coming off a career year with the bat. The big question, however, is whether he can continue being a force at the plate. He set career highs in hits, RBIs, extra-base hits, walks and on-base percentage. He won his third career Gold Glove Award. He has had one other season where he was this good offensively, and it came in 2023 with the Houston Astros. The Orioles could use Dubón in the outfield, or as an option at second base if Jackson Holliday cannot figure things out. Regardless, players in Dubón's tier of free agents are where the Orioles should be expected to shop. He is 32 years old and may not get a long-term deal. However, there is a real possibility that Castillo could find a way to rebound after the worst season of his career and be a monumental pickup for the Rockies. item.description: Henry Cejudo and Eddie Cha celebrate win at UFC 249. | UFC Eddie Cha, one of the sport’s top striking coaches, has suddenly died. Multiple people with knowledge of the situation confirmed to MMA Fighting that Cha passed away at the age of 53. The cause of death is unknown at this time. Cha worked with the likes of Henry Cejudo, Chan Sung Jung, Tracy Cortez, Zhang Weili, Kelvin Gastelum, and many other notable names in the sport of mixed martial arts. A lifelong martial artist, Cha became a full-time coach after a run as a professional poker player, and is known as one of the more positive presences in all of combat sports. Cejudo, who Cha helped coach to UFC world championship gold, reacted to the news on Instagram days before getting ready to face Song Yadong at RAF 15. item.title: Iraola on Rising Star Rio Ngumoha: “We Have to Trust Him Because He Deserves It”
item.description: LIVERPOOL, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 22: Rio Ngumoha of Liverpool is congratulated by Andoni Iraola, Manager of Liverpool, after being substituted off during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Liverpool FC and Manchester United at Anfield on November 22, 2026 in Liverpool, England. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) | Getty Images From the moment he signed for Liverpool in 2024, expectations have been high for Rio Ngumoha to make good on his promise as England’s next star forward. A winger with scintillating pace and tricky technique, if he could put all the pieces together he was always going to be a star. Or at least that was the expectation. This season, at 18 years of age, he very much seems to be putting all of the pieces together. His performance against Manchester United, where his threat led to him regularly being double-marked and still delivering a man of the match calibre performance with a goal and assist, put an exclamation mark on it. “I think not just for Rio, for everyone, the most difficult part is to give a very high level consistently,” head coach Andoni Iraola reflected when asked about the talented young attacker ahead of Wednesday night’s Champions League tie against Club Brugge. “Because maybe you can play a great game, then two or three normal or bad games, and then you have another. Especially in terms of big clubs like Liverpool, the demands are always that you have to be consistent. “This is the most difficult thing for everyone—for us as a team, for every individual player. So with Rio, I always say we have to give him the time to go step by step. We cannot rush it, it wouldn’t be fair with him. But he is in the right mindset, has the right attitude. He is becoming a better and better player.” To date this season, he has made 14 appearances and played 644 minutes out of Liverpool’s 17 games and 1,530 available minutes—meaning he’s played 42% of all available minutes so far. It sets him out as probably the fourth forward for three positions. Most, too, would expect his role to only increase such has been his impact so far. Which is to circle back to the earlier point: 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha very much does seem to be putting it all together in front of our eyes this season. “We know he’s good, but we have to leave him some time also,” Iraola added. Sometimes he’ll have not as good games, will have worse periods, and we still have to trust him because he deserves it because he is very, very good.”

item.title: Grading the Mets’ Paul Goldschmidt signing
item.description: NEW YORK, NY - OCTOBER 07: Paul Goldschmidt #48 of the New York Yankees warms up prior to Game Three of the American League Division Series presented by Booking.com between the Tampa Bay Rays and the New York Yankees at Yankee Stadium on Wednesday, October 7, 2026 in New York, New York. (Photo by Michael Urakami/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images In the aftermath of the Tarik Skubal signing, the Mets turned to the splashiest follow-up possible; signing Paul Goldschmidt to a one-year, $8 million deal with $2 million in potential incentives. Jokes aside, Goldschmidt does fill a clear need for the 2027 Mets, but he comes with some significant questions attached. Older and diminished from both his early-career prime in Arizona and his MVP season for the Cardinals in 2022, Goldschmidt still does a couple things quite well. His primary niche now is as a lefty masher; Goldschmidt posted a 168 wRC+ against southpaws in 2026, good for the 16th best mark in baseball among players with at least 50 PA. He also remains—in an admittedly small sample—an elite defensive first baseman per OAA, a reputation he’s largely carried from his younger days. Now, there are negatives to this. Goldschmidt is an absolute train wreck against right handed pitching, positing a paltry 60 wRC+ largely supported by his peripheral metrics. His bat speed dipped below 71 MPH for the first time since we’ve had publicly available information, all the way down to 69.9 MPH. Correspondingly, both his power and contact skills declined, with his 90th percentile EV dipping below league average and his Z-contact dipping below 77% (a 7th percentile figure). These are all the trends you’d expect from a 39-year-old hitter as he ages, and at this age things can completely go off the cliff at any point. Despite those flaws, this signing makes baseball sense in a vacuum. Jared Young was legitimately good on both sides of the ball once he was given consistent playing time. Pairing him with a lefty-masher who brings similarly high quality defense at first could form an extremely effective platoon if deployed correctly. If nothing else, it’s a massive upgrade over Mark Vientos. There’s a clause in there that’s doing a ton of heavy lifting though; “if deployed correctly”. Goldschmidt should basically never get an at-bat against a right-handed pitcher. He should not be shoehorned into the lineup as the DH on days when there’s a righty on the mound, nor should he receive extended run if Young slumps for any period of time. Goldschmidt is a player with utility, but it’s a very narrow band of utility; deploy him outside of that and things go wrong quickly. Moreover, this is not an easy player to roster in general. Yes, if you’re going to roster a right-hand-hitting 1B/DH who can’t really play anywhere else, you’d rather it be Goldschmidt than Mark Vientos, but really you’d rather just not roster this player at all. item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
